question: How much residual moisture did the water-processed NMC532 cathode lose between 20 °C and drying at 120 °C, and how does its final value compare with the NMP-processed cathode dried at 100 °C?

trace.query: SELECT id, text FROM lines WHERE page IN (8,9) AND (text ILIKE '%moisture%' OR text ILIKE '%ppm%' OR text ILIKE '%120%') ORDER BY id

SELECT (SELECT CAST(regexp_extract(text,'and (\d+) ppm',1) AS INTEGER) FROM lines WHERE id='p8.L54') - (SELECT CAST(regexp_extract(text,'and (\d+) ppm',1) AS INTEGER) FROM lines WHERE id='p8.L59') AS loss_ppm, (SELECT CAST(regexp_extract(text,'and (\d+) ppm',1) AS INTEGER) FROM lines WHERE id='p8.L59') - (SELECT CAST(regexp_extract(text,'reduced to (\d+) ppm',1) AS INTEGER) FROM lines WHERE id='p8.L56') AS diff_vs_nmp

rendered: The water-processed NMC532 cathode held 625 ppm[1] of residual moisture at 20[2] °C. After drying at the higher temperature, 110-120[3] °C (the lower residual value is paired with the upper figure), it held 47 ppm[4] of residual moisture, so it lost 578[5] ppm in total. The NMP-processed cathode dried at 100[6] °C kept 87 ppm[7] of residual moisture, so the water-processed cathode finished with moisture lower by 40[8] ppm than the NMP-processed cathode.
